correctness.rationale: On standard persistent birelational frames, □φ∨¬□φ is valid for every formula and persistent valuation iff x≤y and xRz imply some yRu with u≤z. Sufficiency: if xRz refutes φ, any later y forcing □φ would give u≤z refuting persistence. Necessity: if E fails, take upward-closed valuation V(p)=↑R(y); it forces □p at y but not x, hence forces neither disjunct at x. The explicit two-point poset 0<1 with R={(0,0),(0,1),(1,0)} satisfies base compatibility and E but fails the stronger BEM (missing 1R1). One-point BEM separation impossible. Source verify_small.py enumerates all labeled partial orders and admissible relations at sizes ≤3 (2,34,2942); its exhaustive loops and semantic test were inspected, not used in place of the arbitrary-frame symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating article Lemma 3.1.6 proves only the stronger pointwise successor persistence BEM sufficient; Example 3.1.7 gives a four-point nonconverse but not an exact correspondence. The exact weaker frame condition has existential y-successor lying below z; the two-point witness proves genuine inequivalence and sharpens example size. Resultary searches surfaced other birelational modal classifications, not this E↔Box Excluded Middle. General correspondence theory might subsume the condition, an explicit residual risk.
